recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which nearby value you start from, and the formula you then apply.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Choose the nearby exact point
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the whole choice of method sits here: name x = 1000, Δx = −1 and f′(1000) = 1/300. An examiner reads this line to see whether the nearest perfect cube was found.
lines: Let f(x) = ∛x. Then f(x + Δx) ≈ f(x) + f′(x)·Δx
1000 is the nearest perfect cube to 999, and ∛1000 = 10 exactly

recall.must_convey: That x = 1000 is chosen because ∛1000 = 10 is exact, Δx = −1, and f′(1000) = 1/300.
accept: take x equals one thousand because its cube root is ten
the nearest perfect cube is one thousand so delta x is minus one
f dash of one thousand is one by three hundred
daggara unna perfect cube thousand teesukovali, delta x minus one
start from ten and correct it
heard_as: cube root of thousand is ten

steps.why: The method only works from a point where the function is already known exactly. 1000 is the nearest perfect cube to 999, so the estimate starts at 10 with no calculator, and Δx = −1 is very small next to 1000.
common_mistakes: Choosing x = 999 itself, which leaves the cube root still unknown.
Writing Δx = 1 instead of −1, since 999 is below 1000.
steps.memory_tip: For a cube root, find the nearest whole number whose cube you know; for a square root, the nearest perfect square. Δx carries whatever is left over.

steps.label: Apply the approximation formula
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The correction is 1/300 multiplied by −1, so it is subtracted from 10, not added. A student who writes 10.0033 has used the wrong sign of Δx.

accept: ten minus one by three hundred
ten minus zero point zero zero three three three
the answer is nine point nine nine six seven
ten lo one by three hundred subtract cheyyali
subtract the correction because delta x is negative
heard_as: nine point nine nine six seven
zero point zero zero three three

steps.why: f′(x)·Δx is the correction the tangent line at x = 1000 predicts. The true value is 9.9966656, so this estimate is high by about 0.000001 — the correction is reliable because Δx = −1 is tiny next to 1000.
common_mistakes: Adding the correction instead of subtracting it, giving 10.0033.
steps.memory_tip: New value ≈ old value + slope × step. The step keeps its sign, so a downward move subtracts.

insider_note: Take x = 1000, the nearest perfect cube, giving Δx = −1. f′ = 1/(3(∛x)²) uses the CUBE root squared, which is 100 — not 1000.
